answer.reason: Several verses state events for Kedar: its glory was foretold to fail, Nebuchadrezzar was to smite and spoil it, and its princes traded lambs, rams and goats with Tyre.

clauses.english: was foretold to lose all its glory within a year, its archers diminished
clauses.quote: all the glory of Kedar shall fail

clauses.english: was to be smitten by Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and its tents and flocks taken
clauses.quote: Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east.

clauses.english: traded lambs, rams and goats with Tyre through its princes
clauses.quote: all the princes of Kedar, they occupied with thee in lambs, and rams, and goats

doubts: PSA 120:5 and SNG 1:5 mention the tents of Kedar only as a dwelling and a comparison, so they were left out.
ISA 42:11 and ISA 60:7 are calls to sing and promises of flocks gathered, not events, so they were left out.
The first two clauses rest on prophecies of what was to happen, not on accounts of events that took place.
